spans.text: Eidolos are creatures (and sometimes objects) that have been elevated by the Eidolons, imbued with the ability to act as eidomantic resonators that can channel and bend eidolic radiation. To survive the process of becoming an eidolos a creature must be especially hearty and strong-willed to begin with, so only the most powerful among a species can imagine becoming one. If a creature without the resolve to make the transition is elevated, it is possible they might be destroyed during the process.

Eidolos are ranked into categories that describe their eidolic power - these also determine certain benefits and mechanical powers they have. The four categories (in order of least to most powerful) are oucumenael, pleromael, seraphael and hyperuanael. This rank, combined with the unique soul, history, and powers of an eidolos, are called their cosmogony: a sort of short-hand for a spiritual blueprint that defines the creature, and an abstract “record” of their existence. Through their cosmogony they manifest unique powers, referred to as a cosmic shard and a seraphic authority. Only truly powerful eidolos of seraphael power and higher possess seraphic authority.
Cosmic shards are powers eidolos can invoke, similar to powerful spells. Seraphic authorities are passive effects the eidolos produces simply by existing.

When an eidolos is killed, its body dissolves into nothingness, leaving only an eidolic armament and sepherite behind (see the Eidolic Armament section of this book for more information on them). Sepherite is a special crystal that serves as the core of the eidolos, and is functionally an eidomantic resonator. This sepherite cannot be destroyed except by an eidolic deity, an eidolos of a higher cosmogony rank, or a resplendent constellequary (or by exceptionally powerful beings on par with these things).

3d4 hours after an eidolos is reduced to sepherite, it must attempt a Charisma saving throw with a DC equal to half the damage from the source that destroyed it (or 30 if it was an effect that instantly killed them). The DC decreases by 1 each time the eidolos fails it, and they re-attempt the saving throw every hour after failing. On a success, the eidolos regains its physical form with half of its maximum hit points restored.
Sepherite placed with an
antimagic field
or similar magic-suppressing effect pauses its countdown until its next attempt, and if
dispel magic

is cast on the sepherite then its remaining time between checks is reset to 3d4 hours. The eidolos remains aware of everything happening around it while in sepherite form as though its senses were intact.
If an eidolos is killed by - but not permanently destroyed by - a constellequary, eidolic armament, or eidolic weapon, it loses its ability to restore itself for 1d10 x 10 years.
If an eidolos is permanently destroyed, any eidolic armament it left behind also crumbles into dust.

Eidolos generally begin conceptually as an exiting creature - a basilisk, a red dragon, a gladiator, etc. It is then turned into a unique lifeform by the eidolic deity elevating it, and takes on a new series of abilites/traits along with being assigned a task or responsibility by the eidolic deity that did so. Eidolos possess the following traits and features; when any of the effects below refer to a cosmogony bonus, refer to the table below:

The CR range listed is in reference to the original CR of the creature being created: the CR of a creature becoming an eidolos automatically increases by at least 3, possibly raising its proficiency bonus and statistics. An eidolos must be at least CR 10 by the time they are fully adjusted.

An eidolos will generally resemble a deific/empowered version of its original species, but take on certain specific descriptors. They become associated with a gemstone (their sepherite), which many of the natural minerals in their body are replaced with. Horns, nails, teeth, etc., might be replaced with this gemstone. In many cases the creature’s body may cease being entirely organic, and sections would become an ancient stone-like material, causing an eidolos to resemble an ancient statue or effigy.

Despite this they still exist as they once did: if they could be poisoned before, they can still be. Though they cannot suffocate, if they breathed before they do so now. An eidolos’ body is only a projection of their ideal form from within their sepherite, but the feeling of what they once were causes their body to react the same way it always did.
Eidolos do not age, and can exist forever.

A cosmic shard is a spell-like ability that represents an eidolos’ nature - often it is an offensive ability. When creating them, they should have roughly the same damage or healing potential as the “Creating a Spell” section of the DMG, with effects roughly equivalent to the levels listed on the cosmogony table.

Their Cosmic Shard ability can recharge like features normally would: at the start of an eidolos’ turn, roll a d6. On a result of 4, 5 or 6 the feature is recharged and can be used again. If you want to make a cosmic shard more powerful, you can increase its equivalent spell level in exchange for making the recharge more difficult: one level higher recharges on a 5 or 6, two levels higher recharges on a 6, and three levels higher can only be used once per Long Rest. You may also choose to have a limited number of uses for the ability per Short or Long Rest, and in that case give it three uses per Short or Long Rest, and minus one usage for each spell level higher it is.

In its most basic form, you can choose a spell and appropriate its effects to serve in place of their cosmic shard. Also, if a creature already has a recharging ability such as a breath weapon, you might consider adding effects equivalent to a Cosmic Shard to that instead.
When creating the eidolos Cosmic Shard and/or Seraphic Authority, you should have an equivalent in mind for their eidolic armament if it is produced.

Half of the eidolos’ cosmogony bonus (rounded up) is added to all of their attack rolls, ability checks, initiative checks, damage rolls and saving throws. It gains its full cosmogony bonus as natural armor, adding the bonus on top of its existing armor class.

An eidolos becomes associated with a type of damage, which applies both to it and to the eidolic armaments that come from it. Choose one damage type apart from piercing, slashing or bludgeoning (likely one it could already deal). It becomes immune to that damage type. Its cosmic shard should deal this damage type.
An eidolos’ weapon attacks deal at least one additional damage die, the damage of which is their Cosmogony Damage.
An eidolos’ creature type is the same as its original type, but they also gain the “eidolos (type)” Quality Trait, which is listed in the Quality Trait index. The “type” is its cosmogony type.
An eidolos’ attacks and damage are considered magical and eidolic.

It isn’t marked in their stat blocks, but the resistances, immunities and benefits from their Cosmogony Bonus make eidolos much stronger than their CR would often imply. When an eidolos is defeated in combat, the party defeating them is awarded an extra 50% XP on top of the amount(s) listed in their stat block.
An eidolos has an additional number of hit dice equal to half its normal amount (rounded down). Its hit points are adjusted accordingly.
The eidolos speaks its original languages, as well as Primordial.
An eidolos has at least as many Legendary Resistances as its cosmogony bonus.
If the eidolos fails a saving throw, they can choose to succeed instead. Eidolos possess a number of Legendary Resistances per Long Rest equal to their cosmogony bonus.
Eidolos have advantage on saving throws made against magical effects.
An eidolos is immune to nonmagical piercing, slashing and bludgeoning damage that isn’t eidolic, and resistance to all damage that isn’t eidolic.

Seraphael and hypuranael eidolos gain a seraphic authority: a natural effect the eidolos produces that alters the environment around them, or changes how they interact with it. These effects are passive.
